verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the goal of passing TAP tests on comma-locale Windows has two independent reporters. The open points are fixable design questions. maintenance-fit-2 asks whether public Cluster.pm helpers should exist while a frontend fix that makes them unnecessary is under discussion. maintenance-fit-1 notes that nothing fails on common platforms when a new test skips the helper. demand-1 is weaker, because the change is test-only and costs users nothing.

brief.title: Make TAP tests pass on Windows with comma decimal separator locales
brief.problem: TAP tests fail on Windows machines whose regional settings use a comma as decimal separator, such as Russian. MSVC strtod() takes its locale from Windows regional settings and ignores the LC_NUMERIC=C that PostgreSQL::Test::Utils sets, so psql rejects \watch 0.01 and pg_test_timing prints commas. This affects buildfarm animals and developers with such locales.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds get_decimal_separator() and format_locale_number() to PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster. They detect the decimal separator by asking psql with numericlocale enabled, cache it per node, and format numbers for \watch. pg_test_timing's test regex accepts both '.' and ','.
user_visible_surface: New Perl test methods PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster::get_decimal_separator() and format_locale_number(), available to extension TAP tests.
author_claims: The fix works on the author's Russian-locale Windows 11 box with Strawberry Perl 5.42 and on CI machines.
Accepting [,.] covers most comma locales, including Russian, Brazilian, German, Italian and Polish.
The author calls the fix "ugly" and offers changing the machine locale as an alternative.
brief.thread_state: Thomas Munro suggested reading LC_* variables with getenv() and passing them to setlocale() on Windows; Andrew Bille posted such a frontend patch in a separate thread. Both agree the test fix can go in independently, but nobody has reviewed this patch's code.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether non-test users hit the same \watch failure, which Andrew Bille reports, or whether that is out of scope.
The thread does not say how the patch was found to cover all affected tests.
The proposal does not say what format_locale_number() does with locales whose separator is neither '.' nor ','.
Nobody says whether the tests still pass on Unix with a non-C LC_NUMERIC.
The thread does not say how the test fix interacts with the frontend LC_NUMERIC patch if both are committed.

prior_attempts.title: tsearch and tsdicts regression tests fail in Turkish locale on glibc
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 was about regression tests failing under a Turkish locale on glibc and records no reason. This patch covers TAP tests under comma-decimal locales on Windows.

objections.title: Test API may become dead weight if frontend locale handling changes
objections.failure_scenario: The test helpers ship in a release and extension TAP suites start calling get_decimal_separator(). Later, Andrew Bille's frontend patch makes psql honor LC_NUMERIC=C on Windows, so the helpers always return '.'. Core cannot remove them without breaking the extension tests that call them.
objections.argument: Messages #2, #3 and #5 treat the cause as frontend locale initialization on Windows. Message #3 shows the same \watch failure for real users, and the thread still has an open fix for it. The patch adds public methods to PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster, which extension tests use, to work around behaviour that may change soon. Messages #4 and #5 agree the two fixes are independent, but they do not discuss whether the test-side API should be permanent once the frontend fix lands.
objections.author_must_show: If the frontend fix is committed, can these helpers be removed, and could the test fix be kept private to the affected tests so that extensions do not start depending on them?

critic.reasoning: The patch adds public methods to Cluster.pm, which extension tests can call, while a frontend fix that would make them unnecessary is under discussion. The thread does not say whether the helpers could stay private to the affected tests.

objections.title: New tests with fractional \watch values will silently skip the helper
objections.failure_scenario: A developer later adds a TAP test that runs `\watch 0.1` as a plain literal. It passes on Linux CI and on most Windows animals, then fails only on a comma-locale Windows animal, possibly weeks later. Someone without that setup has to work out the cause and retrofit format_locale_number().
objections.argument: The patch fixes five existing call sites by hand, so every future test that passes a fractional number to psql or parses a frontend's decimal output must remember the helper. On common platforms nothing fails when a test leaves it out. [P6] is a case where a test was removed because carrying platform-specific locale behaviour in tests 'in perpetuity' was judged not worth it. The thread does not say how the five files were found or how new cases would be caught.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a new test that passes a plain fractional literal to psql fail on Linux CI, rather than only on a comma-locale Windows animal?

precedents.title: Revert test case added by commit 1e165d05fe06a9072867607886f818bc255507db.

critic.reasoning: The patch fixes call sites by hand, and nothing on Unix or dot-locale Windows fails when a new test skips the helper. [P6] concerned multiple expected files for a CREATE COLLATION error message, so it should not be used as support.

objections.title: Small affected group with a known workaround; show more demand first
objections.failure_scenario: A test author later adds `\watch 0.5` without format_locale_number(). Every Unix and dot-locale animal stays green. The test breaks only on a comma-locale Windows box, which the patch exists to support. That box may be one machine, and its owner can switch Windows regional settings to a dot locale.
objections.argument: The demand shown is two developers with Russian-locale Windows machines (messages #1, #3) and one planned buildfarm animal. Message #1 offers changing the machine locale as an alternative and calls the fix "ugly". Andrew Bille's frontend LC_NUMERIC patch (messages #3, #5) would fix both the `\watch` failure and pg_test_timing output, which would make the new Cluster.pm helpers unnecessary. [P6] records the same judgement: carrying test machinery for Windows locale variation was not worth it once the code path worked.
objections.author_must_show: How many buildfarm animals or developers run Windows with comma decimal locales, and why should the helpers stay if the frontend LC_NUMERIC fix is committed?

precedents.title: Revert test case added by commit 1e165d05fe06a9072867607886f818bc255507db.

critic.reasoning: Two independent reports show some demand, but message #1 itself says a dot-decimal regional setting would do the job, and the thread does not weigh that against permanent helpers. [P6] is about expected files for an error message and should not be used as support.

refuted.title: Ongoing cost of locale-aware test helpers for one setup
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a TAP test that passes a literal `\watch 0.5` without format_locale_number(). It passes on CI and Unix buildfarm animals, then fails only on a comma-locale Windows animal. That animal's owner, not the patch author, ends up tracing it to the helper that was not used.
refuted.argument: [P6] removed a locale-dependent test because supporting several platform behaviors was not worth carrying in perpetuity, and here the patch makes every future fractional \watch test depend on such support. Message #1 calls the fix "ugly" and says switching the machine to a dot locale is an option. Messages #3 and #5 propose a frontend fix that would make the helper unnecessary. The thread does not yet weigh a permanent test API against requiring a C-like numeric locale on Windows animals.
refuted.author_must_show: Why carry get_decimal_separator() permanently instead of documenting that Windows buildfarm animals need a dot-decimal locale until the frontend fix lands?

precedents.title: Revert test case added by commit 1e165d05fe06a9072867607886f818bc255507db.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which gives the same forgotten-helper scenario under the more exact rubric item. The point about switching the machine locale is covered by demand-1.

refuted.title: Tests adapt to locale-dependent \watch parsing instead of flagging it
refuted.failure_scenario: A user writes a psql script containing `\watch 0.5` and runs it on a Windows machine with Russian regional settings. psql rejects the interval. With this patch the TAP tests pass on that machine because they send `0,5`, so no test shows that the same script behaves differently on different machines.
refuted.argument: Message #3 and message #5 show that the `\watch` failure is user-visible. Every other number a psql script contains, such as a SQL literal, uses '.', whatever the locale. The patch turns the locale-dependent spelling into what the tests expect, and it adds get_decimal_separator() and format_locale_number() to the shared Cluster.pm API, where extension tests can come to rely on it. Message #4 treats the frontend question as separate, but the test helper takes a position on it now.
refuted.author_must_show: Should `\watch` accept a locale-formatted interval at all, and if not, why should the shared test API format numbers that way instead of keeping the tests strict?

critic.reasoning: psql rejects `\watch 0.5` under a comma locale today, so the patch does not cause the scenario. Messages #4 and #5 agree that the frontend behavior is a separate question, and it has its own thread.

refuted.title: New Cluster.pm helpers duplicate the LC_NUMERIC=C setting in Utils.pm
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension author uses format_locale_number() in TAP tests. Later the frontend LC_NUMERIC patch lands, LC_NUMERIC=C takes effect on Windows, and the helper becomes dead weight that cannot be removed without breaking those extension tests. Meanwhile psql users still see \watch 0.01 rejected, and no test catches it.
refuted.argument: Utils.pm already forces LC_NUMERIC=C so that numbers in tests use a period. The patch keeps that setting and adds a second path that detects the separator per node and formats numbers around it. Messages #3 and #5 show the root cause is that frontends ignore LC_NUMERIC on Windows, and that the frontend patch fixes both pg_test_timing and \watch. All agreed the test fix need not wait, but nothing in the thread says the new helpers are wanted as a lasting public test API.
refuted.author_must_show: If the frontend LC_NUMERIC patch is committed, would these helpers be removed, and could they stay private to the affected tests until then?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, with the same scenario and the same question to the author. The duplication claim is also weak, because message #1 shows that LC_NUMERIC=C has no effect on MSVC strtod().

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds public methods get_decimal_separator() and format_locale_number() to PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster, which extension TAP tests can call.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: A buildfarm animal also runs back branches, and the proposal does not say whether the test fix goes there.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every future test that passes a fractional number to psql must use the helper, and only comma-locale Windows machines show an omission.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: A frontend LC_NUMERIC patch in a separate thread, or a dot-decimal regional setting, would solve the same failures without test helpers.

questions: If the frontend LC_NUMERIC patch is committed, can these helpers be removed, and could they stay private to the affected tests until then?
What makes a new test that passes a plain fractional literal to psql fail on Linux CI, instead of only on a comma-locale Windows animal?
How were the five touched test files found, and does a full TAP run on the Russian-locale machine pass with the patch?
What does format_locale_number() return on a locale whose decimal separator is neither '.' nor ','?
How many buildfarm animals or developers run Windows with a comma decimal locale, and why is a dot-decimal regional setting not enough for them?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the TAP test framework and Windows locale behaviour of the frontends. Thomas Munro commented on the cause in message #2, but nobody has reviewed the patch.
committability.liability: Two public test methods in Cluster.pm that extension tests may come to call, plus follow-up fixes each time a new test skips the helper. The liability lasts until a frontend fix makes the helpers unnecessary, and longer if extensions use them.
committability.author_follow_up: The author registered the CommitFest entry in August 2026 and posted again in September 2026, so the author is still active on the thread.

priority.reason: The patch is 5.8 KB, changes only test files, and helps developers and buildfarm animals on comma-locale Windows. The scope of the helpers should be settled against the frontend LC_NUMERIC patch before code review.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the caching of the detected separator, the behaviour on Unix with a non-C LC_NUMERIC, and the handling of other separators could not be checked. Messages #4 and #5 were not shown in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Mitigation for mutating locale names on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a user-editable locale name map file, setlocale.map, that win32setlocale.c reads to rename locale names before calling setlocale(), so a cluster whose Windows locale was renamed by an OS update (Turkish_Turkey to Turkish_Türkiye) can start again. It also moves the built-in rename table into this mechanism and adds a debug build option to test the mapping on Unix.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author, Thomas Munro, withdrew the patch after learning in another thread that Windows "Locale Builder" can already fix a renamed locale for an existing database, so he did not want to maintain the map file. The install crash was traced to a different cause: the EDB installer passes a non-ASCII locale name that makes the Windows runtime crash. No Windows user had tested the patch across the real upgrade.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: We don't really need the "setlocale.map" rename-on-the-fly patch in this thread, and I don't want to maintain it if we don't need it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track collation and ctype versions separately
precedents_retrieved.summary: Track the ctype version (in effect the Unicode version) separately from the collation version, in pg_collation and pg_database, so that changes to case mapping and pattern matching can be detected. The thread also asked whether the growing set of locale fields in pg_database should be cleaned up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took it up, and the author withdrew the patch for lack of discussion. Before that, the author noted that the extra field is confusing, because in pg_database it holds the ctype version of the default collation and not necessarily that of datctype.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm withdrawing this patch due to a lack of discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow HAVE_UCOL_STRCOLLUTF8 flag to be set conditionally on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the Windows MSVC build scripts so that HAVE_UCOL_STRCOLLUTF8 is set only when the ICU version supports it, by running uconv from the configured ICU bin path to detect the version. The thread started from a server crash in varstr_cmp() when ICU collations were used on Windows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: A different fix made the patch unnecessary. Peter Eisentraut committed a change that stops using ucol_strcollUTF8() on ICU versions before 53 and replaces the existing configure test with one that also works on Windows. Peter Geoghegan and Peter Eisentraut then agreed that this ended the Windows issue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: He committed it just now, so that's the end of this Windows issue, I suppose.

precedents_retrieved.title: make psql backslash commands honor "\pset null"
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the special handling of NULL values in psql backslash commands, which set nullPrint = NULL in src/bin/psql/describe.c. Commands such as \dp would then honor "\pset null", so a NULL ACL (default privileges) can be told apart from an empty one.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch on the day he posted it, after he saw that a conflicting proposal existed and said he would reply on that thread. No one objected to the patch in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I just realize that there is a conflicting proposal.

precedents_retrieved.title: Windows Service status is set to "SERVICE_RUNNING" when timeout is occurred (version 9.6 or earlier).
precedents_retrieved.summary: On PostgreSQL 9.6 and earlier, a Windows service registered with pg_ctl -w ends in the STOPPED state when startup times out during long crash recovery, even though the server keeps running. The first patch set the service status to SERVICE_RUNNING after such a timeout; a later patch by another author set it to SERVICE_START_PENDING when the postmaster was still starting.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tsunakawa questioned the first approach: whether SERVICE_RUNNING is correct for a server that has not finished startup, and whether the problem also affects version 10 and later. He also commented on the new messages. The replacement patch, which used SERVICE_START_PENDING, was judged by the original patch author not to fix the reported problem, because nothing would later change the status to SERVICE_RUNNING once recovery finished. The visible thread has no reply or revised patch after that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think no one could change the service status to SERVICE_RUNNING even if the server has been started properly after timeout is occurred.

precedents_retrieved.title: Introduce list_reverse() to make lcons() usage less inefficient
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a list_reverse() function so that generate_orderedappend_paths() can lappend() child paths and reverse the list once, instead of using lcons(). Since Lists became arrays, lcons() moves every existing element on each call, so building the list this way costs quadratic time with many partitions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund suggested an alternative: iterate over the partition children in reverse order when match_partition_order_desc is set, with no list reversal at all. The author agreed, wrote an open-coded reverse loop with similar planning time, pushed that patch instead, and withdrew list_reverse().
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But wouldn't an even cheaper way here be to iterate over the children in
reverse order when match_partition_order_desc?

precedents_retrieved.title: lc_messages parameter doesn't work on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets the gettext LANGUAGE environment variable on Windows so that the lc_messages setting selects the message language there, as it does on other platforms. The author called it a workaround and also raised mixed log encodings when databases on one server use different encodings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Noah Misch could not reproduce the problem: with Postgres 11 beta3 binaries on Windows Server 2016, LC_MESSAGES already switched the psql message language. He asked for output with and without the patch and for the Windows, gettext and locale details. The author did not answer, and Dmitry Dolgov returned the patch for age and lack of answers to the review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Due to age and lack of answers to the reviewers feedback, I think it's right to
mark this patch as "Returned with feedback", unless someone is interested and
wants to take over it.

implementation of stat() in this build context, but I am not sure either
if relying on the implementation of stat() in MinGW to take care of the
problems we are trying to fix is enough or not.  So this needs more
study.
